diagnostics.message: The runner instance's user-data is responsible for writing the registration token into the SSM parameter named by local.secure_parameter_store_runner_token_key, but nothing references aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token. Terraform may create/boot the launch configuration (and hence the instance running user-data) before the parameter exists, and a later apply can clobber the token the instance wrote. aws_launch_configuration.gitlab_runner_instance should depend on aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token.

When cloudwatch logging is enabled the instance user-data configures logging against the log group whose name equals var.environment, which is exactly aws_cloudwatch_log_group.environment. The launch configuration/user-data has no dependency on that log group, so the instance may boot before the group exists (and the on-host agent can auto-create an unmanaged group that later conflicts with the Terraform-managed one). aws_launch_configuration.gitlab_runner_instance should depend on aws_cloudwatch_log_group.environment.

local_file.public_ssh_key's `content` already references tls_private_key.ssh.public_key_openssh, so the explicit `depends_on = ["tls_private_key.ssh"]` duplicates an ordering Terraform already infers and can be removed.

local_file.private_ssh_key's `content` already references tls_private_key.ssh.private_key_pem, so the explicit `depends_on = ["tls_private_key.ssh"]` duplicates an ordering Terraform already infers and can be removed.
